newsitem.title: UK: Bradford wooltops move higher ahead of merino sale.
newsitem.headline: Bradford wooltops move higher ahead of merino sale.

text.p: Sellers of finer tops pushed for higher prices on Monday, taking advantage of market opinion that Australian raw wool values will sustain their recent firmness in the immediate term, industry sources said.
"Everyone says there is rigid resistance among customers to paying more but that if wool is seen to cost more from week to week, it may gradually be overcome," one said.
Most tops were quoted up by two to five pence per kg with the exception of English-woolled tops which were quoted unchanged.
A softer tendency in the pound against the U.S. dollar served to exaggerate the rise in merino prices.
Although the outlook for the dollar is uncertain, topmakers noted the risks of becoming oversold at prices subject to currency movements.

Sources in Western Europe said there were no signs of recovery after the industry downturn and added that pressure from governments seeking to meet the economic preconditions for European Monetary Union were adding to trading difficulties.
